# Awesome Sign Languages

[![Awesome](https://awesome.re/badge.svg)](https://awesome.re)

[Português (Brasil)](README.pt-BR.md) | **English**

A curated directory of high-quality sign language resources: dictionaries, learning materials, linguistic references, corpora, and software. Sign languages are full natural languages with their own grammars and communities—not universal versions of spoken languages. They must be named precisely: **Libras** is the Brazilian Sign Language, used in Brazil, and is distinct from Portuguese and from other sign languages.

This list is intentionally selective. Inclusion is based on clear provenance, usefulness, and fit for the stated purpose, not popularity or search ranking. A resource can be free to access without its data being free to download or reuse; check each project's terms.

> **Language-specific starting point:** This English version presents ASL resources first. For a Portuguese-language guide that presents Libras resources first, use the [Português (Brasil) version](README.pt-BR.md). The language of this document is not a translation direction: ASL and Libras are different languages.

## Learning and teaching

### American Sign Language (ASL)

- [ASL Connect – ASL by Topic](https://gallaudet.edu/asl-connect/topics/) - Free basic American Sign Language (ASL) vocabulary videos and self-paced lessons from Gallaudet University. Vocabulary support, not a substitute for interactive instruction.
- [Learning American Sign Language](https://clerccenter.gallaudet.edu/ndec/educational-resources/learning-asl/) - Clerc Center's guide to learning ASL, classes, and educational resources; explains the language's grammar and why in-person community practice matters.

## Dictionaries and lexical resources

### American Sign Language (ASL)

- [ASL Signbank](https://aslsignbank.com/) - Research-maintained ASL lexical resource from University of Connecticut and Gallaudet University. Public users can browse signs and translation equivalents; some data requires registration and approval. Intended for fluent signers and linguistic annotation, not a beginner course.
- [ASL-LEX](https://asl-lex.org/) - Research database documenting lexical and phonological properties of 2,723 ASL signs, with video references and searchable visualizations. Database reuse is noncommercial (CC BY-NC 4.0); reference videos are excluded from that license.

## Linguistics and reference

### American Sign Language (ASL)

- [The Linguistics of American Sign Language](https://gupress.gallaudet.edu/Books/L/Linguistics-of-American-Sign-Language2) - Gallaudet University Press textbook on ASL structure and linguistics (fifth edition). A scholarly reference; the book is not a free resource.
- [Sign Language Annotation, Archiving and Sharing (SLAASh)](https://gallaudet.edu/american-sign-language/sign-language-annotation-archiving-and-sharing-slaash/) - Gallaudet project and conventions supporting sign language video annotation, archiving, and sharing.

## Corpora and datasets

### American Sign Language (ASL)

- [YouTube-ASL](https://github.com/google-research/google-research/tree/master/youtube_asl) - Google Research dataset of ASL videos with English captions, reviewed by Deaf annotators for video quality and caption alignment. The release provides video IDs, not the videos; availability, caption quality, and platform rights can vary. See the project paper and terms before research use.
- [OpenASL](https://github.com/chevalierNoir/OpenASL) - Research dataset and code for open-domain ASL-to-English translation. Access and reuse are subject to its noncommercial, no-derivatives license; check the repository for current terms and dataset limitations.

## Software and research tools

### General-purpose

- [ELAN](https://archive.mpi.nl/mpi/elan) - Professional annotation tool for audio and video, widely used in language research and compatible with sign language lexicons such as ASL Signbank. Free and open source under GPL-3.0; review its license and documentation.

## Libras resources

The resources below cover **Libras (Brazilian Sign Language)**. They are grouped here so learners, researchers, families, and developers do not mistake ASL materials or Portuguese-language interfaces for Libras resources. Most entries are in Portuguese, because that is the language of the Brazilian Deaf community's institutions; the entries explain what each one offers.

> Links checked on **2 October 2026**. Not every deaf or hard-of-hearing person in Brazil uses Libras; this list covers resources **in and about Libras**.

### Free Libras courses

- [Introdução à Libras — Escola Virtual.Gov](https://www.escolavirtual.gov.br/curso/11) - 60-hour course from Enap with content from Brazil's Ministry of Human Rights and Citizenship. Open, free, and certified; anyone can enroll and has 60 days to finish. Covers Deaf culture, legislation, fingerspelling, numbers, classifiers, and basic vocabulary.
- [LibrasEdu — IFRO MOOC](https://mooc.ifro.edu.br/mod/page/view.php?id=858) - Open online course from the Federal Institute of Rondônia, free for everyone. Approved participants issue their digital certificate within the platform.
- [Libras I — Mundi, IFSul](https://mundi.ifsul.edu.br/portal/libras-I.php) - 40-hour beginner course with no prerequisites on IFSul's free online course platform: four modules on Deaf culture and identity, fingerspelling, numbers, introductions, classifiers, and basic sign lists.
- [Introdução aos estudos da Libras — PoCA, UFSCar](https://cursos.poca.ufscar.br/local/staticpage/view.php?page=49) - 30-hour course on UFSCar's open-course portal: Deaf studies, sociocultural views of deafness, grammar basics, and first steps in communication. Check the course page for certificate terms.
- [Comunicação para TODOS — Lúmina, UFRGS](https://lumina.ufrgs.br/course/view.php?id=593) - Free 10-hour course in Portuguese and Libras on communication accessibility tools. This offering does not issue a certificate.

Online courses help you start but do not replace time with the Deaf community. For fluency, seek classes and events with fluent Deaf signers.

### Deaf creators

Free content in Libras. For YouTube channels we checked for recent uploads. A creator is described as Deaf only when they say so on their channel or a news article states it.

- [Isflocos — Gabriel Isaac](https://www.youtube.com/@isflocos) - Gabriel Isaac introduces himself on the channel as Deaf, a multi-artist, and a content creator; he talks about Deaf life and culture. [News profile](https://jornalarua.com/2025/10/22/influencer-de-sp-gabriel-isaac-abre-os-planos-para-a-cultura-surda-no-brasil-em-2026/).
- [Léo Viturinno](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCR_-CWbo1ZhNsQLyzKJL7DA) - Deaf creator (per [this list](https://blog.inboarding.co/12-canais-de-youtube-em-libras/)). Vlogs, films and series, culture, and a "Curso Básico de Libras" lesson series, captioned in Portuguese.
- [Fábio de Sá TV](https://www.youtube.com/@FabiodesaTV) - Channel of Fábio de Sá, who describes himself as a Deaf poet, Visual Vernacular artist, actor, narrator, and Libras teacher. Videos in Libras.
- [Tikinho Ramon](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UC4-wQT4oiakr0WtwaxN8DoQ) - Lucas Ramon, a Deaf designer and cartoonist (per [this list](https://blog.inboarding.co/12-canais-de-youtube-em-libras/)); shares his drawings, exhibitions, and travels.
- [Nathalia da Silva](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCx_js_0y1GOpSnM7v4h5Xrg) - Deaf creator (per [this list](https://blog.inboarding.co/12-canais-de-youtube-em-libras/)) with beauty and everyday-life videos.

### Institutions and projects

- [INES — official channel](https://www.youtube.com/@ines.oficial) - Channel of the National Institute of Deaf Education with institutional videos such as events and admissions information in Libras.
- [Libras e Saúde — UFSC](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UC3Ge3vQ6r-j6VKnWaTl76AQ) - UFSC project with Libras videos, captioned in Portuguese, on health (Brazil's public health system, vaccination, hypertension, diabetes, and more) for Deaf signers. See the [project page](https://librasesaude.paginas.ufsc.br/producoes/inicio/).
- [Na Palma da Mão — UFES](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCBsQvVszGY7KdxvbUCMRHfg) - Channel of UFES's LISIT research group with education, culture, health, and legal content in Libras.
- [DLibras — UNIR](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UC2C0o7Elijx39JkAY6I_BXg) - Channel of the Libras Department at the Federal University of Rondônia, including the accessible [podcast "Um minuto, um direito delas"](https://www.unir.br/cartao/exibir/298).
- [IFRS em Libras](https://ifrs.edu.br/ifrs-em-libras/) - Federal Institute of Rio Grande do Sul channel with institutional information, admissions, teaching materials, and glossaries in Libras.
- [Canal Libras — MEC](https://www.gov.br/mec/pt-br/canal-libras) - Ministry of Education channel with programming for Deaf audiences, from early childhood through higher education.
- [TV INES (archive)](https://debasi.ines.gov.br/tv-ines) - Archive of Brazil's first web TV in Libras (launched 24 April 2013), with captions and Portuguese voice-over. Programs on education, interviews, humor, and children's content remain available; the TV no longer produces new content.

### Libras lessons alongside paid courses

- [Moreno Libras](https://www.youtube.com/@morenolibras) - Active Libras lessons channel. Offers free lessons on YouTube and also sells courses.

### Learning and sharing

- [DEBASI — INES Basic Education](https://debasi.ines.gov.br/) - Site of INES's school of application with bilingual materials for Deaf children, teenagers, and adults: activities, Libras storybook videos, sign lists, projects, and TV INES videos.
- [Repositório Digital do INES](http://repositorio.ines.gov.br/ilustra/) - Instituto Nacional de Educação de Surdos (INES) repository of Libras educational materials. Browse the metadata and license for each item before downloading or reusing it; formats and accessibility features vary by resource.
- [Manuário Acadêmico e Escolar](https://manuario.ines.gov.br/) - INES's subject-organized collection of Libras signs for school and academic contexts. Its signs are collected, validated with Deaf INES teachers and academic-community representatives, then recorded in studio; useful for specialized vocabulary, not a complete general dictionary.

### Dictionaries and lexical documentation

- [Dicionário da Língua Brasileira de Sinais — INES](https://dicionario.ines.gov.br/) - Searchable Libras dictionary from INES with videos, Portuguese examples and senses, subjects, grammatical classes, and sign-origin information.
- [Dicionário de Libras — UFV](https://sistemas.cead.ufv.br/capes/dicionario/) - Online dictionary from the Federal University of Viçosa with basic regional signs. Search by word, topic, sign list, or handshape.
- [Signbank Libras](https://signbank.levantelab.com.br/pt/about) - UFSC-linked, open-access Libras signbank connected to the Global Signbank and Libras Corpus. Supports lexical and linguistic research and can link to ELAN; it is a research lexicon rather than a prescriptive authority for every regional variant.

Libras has regional variation, like any language. If a sign differs from what you know, ask Deaf signers from your region.

### Books, journals, and bilingual materials

- [Centro Virtual de Cultura Surda — UFF](https://libras.uff.br/centro-virtual-de-cultura-surda/) - With Editora Arara Azul, free e-books on teaching Libras as a first language, teacher and interpreter training, lexicon, and translation, plus a scientific journal, academic notebooks, and a digital library with Libras literature and adapted classics. The site also has a glossary and video lessons.
- [Editora Arara Azul](https://editora-arara-azul.com.br/e-books/) - Publisher of materials on bilingual education, Libras, and Deaf Studies. Its e-book page points to the UFF site above.
- [Portal de Publicações do INES](https://seer.ines.gov.br/) - Open-access portal for journals, books, and materials published by INES.
- [Revista Espaço — INES](https://seer.ines.gov.br/index.php/revista-espaco) - INES academic journal (founded 1990) on Deaf education, Libras, Deaf literature, and language policy.
- [Publicações do INES — gov.br](https://www.gov.br/ines/pt-br/central-de-conteudos/publicacoes-1/todas-as-publicacoes) - List of INES institutional publications, including bilingual pedagogy materials.

### Institutions, rights, and dates

- [INES — National Institute of Deaf Education](https://www.gov.br/ines/pt-br) - Federal reference institution for Deaf education, founded in 1857 and part of the Ministry of Education.
- [FENEIS — National Federation of Deaf Education and Integration](https://feneis.org.br/o-que-e/) - Nonprofit founded in 1987 that defends language policy, education, culture, employment, health, and rights of the Brazilian Deaf community, with regional offices in several states.
- [Lei nº 10.436/2002 — Libras Law](https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/leis/2002/l10436.htm) - Recognizes Libras as a legal means of communication and expression of Brazil's Deaf communities.
- [Decreto nº 5.626/2005](https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2004-2006/2005/decreto/d5626.htm) - Regulates the Libras Law: Libras in schools, teacher and interpreter training, and services for Deaf people.
- [Lei nº 14.191/2021 — Bilingual Deaf education](https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2019-2022/2021/lei/L14191.htm) - Adds bilingual Deaf education to Brazil's education law: Libras as first language, written Portuguese as second.

- **24 April — National Libras Day** ([Lei nº 13.055/2014](https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2011-2014/2014/lei/l13055.htm)) and **26 September — National Deaf People's Day** ([Lei nº 11.796/2008](https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2007-2010/2008/lei/L11796.htm)). September is "Setembro Azul" campaign month; see [how FENEIS marks Deaf Day](https://feneis.org.br/feneis-celebra-o-dia-do-surdo-com-orgulho/).

### Linguistics, corpora, and datasets

- [Corpus de Libras](https://corpuslibras.ufsc.br/?lang=en) - UFSC's openly accessible Libras corpus with video, photos, data, metadata, and documentation guidelines. Designed for linguistic research, professional work, and preservation; follow its access conditions and participant/data-use guidance.

### Software, access, and collaboration

- [Suíte VLibras](https://www.gov.br/governodigital/pt-br/acessibilidade-e-usuario/vlibras) - Brazilian government and UFPB/LAVID free, open-source accessibility suite that automatically renders digital Portuguese content in Libras with a 3D avatar. Includes web, desktop, and mobile tools.
- [VLibras Widget documentation](https://vlibras.gov.br/doc/widget/introduction/presentation.html) - Official integration guide for adding the Portuguese-to-Libras accessibility widget to a website.
- [WikiLibras](https://wiki.vlibras.gov.br/) - Collaborative VLibras platform for consulting signs and proposing or reviewing signs, translations, and avatar animations. Contributions enter the suite only after its expert review process.
- [Hand Talk App](https://www.handtalk.me/br/aplicativo/) - Brazilian app that translates text and speech from Portuguese into Libras with the Hugo and Maya avatars, with a dictionary and a learning path ("Hands Up") that the company says is made by Deaf educators, linguists, and CODAs. Free with an optional subscription; translation is automatic.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> VLibras and Hand Talk render content **from Portuguese to Libras** with avatars; they are not bidirectional Portuguese–Libras interpreters and do not replace a human interpreter. They should not be the sole access provision in classes, legal proceedings, health care, public-service interactions, or other high-stakes communication. Verify regional and contextual appropriateness with Libras users.

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome, especially resources for sign languages and communities underrepresented here, and channels and projects led by Deaf people.

The easiest way is the [suggestion form](https://github.com/tbalbinodesa/awesome-sign-languages/issues/new?template=sugerir-recurso.yml) (a GitHub account is needed; no Markdown knowledge is). You can also open an issue or pull request. Include:

- The resource's official URL and the specific sign language(s) it covers.
- Who maintains it and why it is trustworthy (for example, a Deaf-led organization, university, established research team, or transparent community project).
- What it offers, who it is for, and whether it is free to access.
- Any restrictions on accounts, downloads, redistribution, commercial use, or data licensing.
- Evidence of quality and currency; flag known limitations such as dialect coverage, incomplete entries, or machine-generated content.

Do not submit scraped content, unverified sign translation apps, or claims that a resource translates between “sign language” and speech without naming the languages and explaining its limitations. A sign language is not universal; list each language explicitly. For automatic translation tools, state the supported direction(s), whether output is avatar-based or human-produced, and that it does not replace interpreting. Access does not imply permission to redistribute.

Want to help spread the word to the Brazilian Deaf community? See the [outreach plan](docs/divulgacao.md) (in Portuguese).
